content: Customer was charged twice for the same month. Investigation found a retry on a failed payment that also succeeded. Resolution: one charge refunded to the original card, processed in 5 business days. Customer confirmed.
Customer asked for a refund 20 days after an annual charge, outside the 14-day window. Resolution: not refundable per policy; plan stays active until the period ends. Offered a downgrade at renewal.
Customer locked out after several failed sign-in attempts. Resolution: confirmed identity, cleared the lock early, sent a password reset link. Advised the lock clears on its own after 30 minutes.

Customer wanted to change the sign-in email but the new address never got the confirmation link. Resolution: link had expired; resent it; change completed once the customer clicked the new link within 60 minutes.
Customer upgraded mid-cycle and asked why they were charged immediately. Resolution: explained upgrades take effect at once with a pro-rated charge for the rest of the period. Customer satisfied.
Customer removed two seats and expected an instant refund. Resolution: removed seats free up at the next billing period, no mid-cycle refund. Confirmed the seat count drops at renewal.
Hardware add-on tracking showed delivered but customer did not receive it. Resolution: reported within the 7-day window, confirmed as missing, replacement shipped at no cost via express.
Customer hit error code E-402 and thought it was a billing fault. Resolution: E-402 is an expired session, not billing. Signing out and back in cleared it.
Customer reported sync stuck on a single item. Resolution: opened the item, made a small edit, saved again to force a re-sync. Item synced correctly afterward.

Customer asked to move data to a different region after account creation. Resolution: region cannot be changed in place; raised a data migration request. Explained the 30-day grace period for deletions separately.
